FO:3 wasn't quite as consistent as NV, but I'd say the high marks were higher. FO:3 had a bunch of ridiculous vaults to explore. And ThreeDog was a pretty entertaining radio DJ. I also prefer Megaton as the main city over The Strip (The Strip may be better than Tenpenny Tower though). That said, the many competing factions made the main story in NV a bit more interesting. As for random exploration they both have their pluses and minuses. FO:3 biggest problem was the sprawling urban ruin, subway trawl, that while fun and labyrinthine at times, could be awfully same-y and repetitive some other times. NV on the other hand was a lot more open (muuuch easier to get from point A to B) but as a result the world sometimes felt a bit more empty.

FO:4 does have a number of songs from FO:3, whereas NV has it's own, more country-esque soundtrack. FO:3 has an annoying bug where a save may be corrupted (albeit rarely) while NV has an annoying bug where certain saves won't load if they're the first save loaded since launching, and once it triggers on a save it won't stop (meaning I'd have to start sessions by starting a new game, then loading my most recent save). So neither is a clear winner in the bugs department.

As for character progression, they're fairly similar, though FO:3 feels a bit more balanced, or less cheesy for min-maxing, due to how the extra SPECIAL points are obtained. In FO:3 there is a bobblehead for each SPECIAL stat somewhere in the world, so you have to do things to get them. In NV, you spend your caps at the doctor's office to get the enhancements you want in whatever order you want. And you can get all the caps you want by using quick saves to cheese the money making process at casinos (if that's how you roll). NV maybe has some interesting side-things to collect though: namely those star bottlecaps. Kept me drinking my Sunset Saspirilla's whereas in FO:3 I'd usually just vendor my Nuka Colas.

You'll enjoy either, and they're both worth playing IMO.

Fallout NV all the way. It has

  • an infinitely better story (mind you that Obsidian has many people from Black Isle, who developed the original two Fallout games)

  • more and better in-game companions, more (and for the most part, better) quests,

  • more factions that actually are believable rather than being the boring Black & White BoS vs. Enclave of Fallout 3

  • more weapons (most of whom can be modified), different ammunition types such as armor-piercing and hollow-point rounds

  • more emphasis on stats and skills (with more frequent stat/skill checks)

  • better DLCs (though Dead Money is very hit and miss. Gun Runner's Arsenal doesn't count).

  • from my impression, better mods (i.e. the DLC-sized Project Brazil, the extremely good quest mod Autumn Leaves, and the massive dungeon mod A World of Pain)

  • An in-built (but optional) hardcore mod where you regularly have to drink, eat, and sleep or stat damage or death, amongst other things.

The only thing Fallout 3 has over NV is a slightly larger map and more dungeons to explore. Unlike it's FO3's botched story, you can actually fix these shortcomings of NV can easily be fixed by slapping a few mods on it. As for NV being buggy - yep, sadly that's the case, but FO3 is none the better in that regard, nor is any other title running on the GameBryo engine.
